name: Historic Center (Centro Histórico)
shortDescription: Colonial streets, plazas, and cultural landmarks in the heart of Santa Marta.
longDescription: A walkable district packed with historic architecture, museums, churches, and plazas. Best explored on foot, especially in the late afternoon and evening.

name: Parque de los Novios
shortDescription: Classic social hub with cafés, bars, and evening energy.
longDescription: A lively meeting point in the historic center, popular for dinner, drinks, and people-watching. Great starting point for a night out.
address: Parque de los Novios, Centro, Santa Marta

name: Marina Santa Marta
shortDescription: Waterfront marina with bay views and a breezy promenade.
longDescription: A scenic spot for a calm walk and photos, especially around sunset. Nearby you’ll find restaurants and the bayfront walkway.
address: Marina Santa Marta, Centro, Santa Marta

name: Santa Marta Public Market (Mercado Público)
shortDescription: Local market for produce, snacks, and everyday city flavor.
longDescription: A practical and vibrant stop to see local ingredients and quick eats. Best visited in the morning for peak activity.

name: Catedral Basílica de Santa Marta
shortDescription: Iconic cathedral in the historic center.
longDescription: A landmark church worth a visit for architecture, history, and its central location for exploring nearby plazas and streets.

name: Museo del Oro Tairona (Casa de la Aduana)
shortDescription: Museum highlighting Tayrona heritage and regional history.
longDescription: A must for cultural context, with exhibits connected to Indigenous history and the region’s past. Easy to combine with a historic center walk.
address: Casa de la Aduana, Centro, Santa Marta

name: Quinta de San Pedro Alejandrino
shortDescription: Historic estate and museum with shaded gardens.
longDescription: A calm cultural visit with museum spaces and garden paths. One of the most important historic sites in Santa Marta.
address: Quinta de San Pedro Alejandrino, Santa Marta

name: Terminal de Transportes Santa Marta
shortDescription: Main bus terminal for regional routes and transfers.
longDescription: Key transport hub for intercity buses and connections. Useful when traveling to nearby towns and destinations.

name: Simón Bolívar International Airport (SMR)
shortDescription: Santa Marta’s main airport for domestic connections.
longDescription: Primary entry point by air. Taxis and transfers connect the airport with the city and beach zones.
address: Aeropuerto Internacional Simón Bolívar, Santa Marta

name: El Rodadero Beach
shortDescription: Famous beach area with broad sands and lots of services.
longDescription: A classic beach day spot with restaurants, vendors, and nearby attractions. Very convenient and busy during peak hours.

name: Playa Blanca (Rodadero)
shortDescription: Boat-access beach with clear water near El Rodadero.
longDescription: A popular day-trip beach typically reached by boat from Rodadero. Go early to enjoy calmer water and fewer crowds.

name: Rodadero Sea Aquarium and Museum
shortDescription: Aquarium and marine museum across from El Rodadero.
longDescription: A family-friendly visit to learn about marine life and enjoy exhibits. Often combined with boat trips in the area.

name: Ensenada Inca Inca
shortDescription: Small cove area associated with nearby boat routes and attractions.
longDescription: A coastal cove zone near Rodadero used as a reference point for nearby attractions and boat access.

name: Morro de Gaira (Isla Pelícano)
shortDescription: Small offshore islet visible from Rodadero bay.
longDescription: A distinctive natural landmark in the bay, often referenced during boat rides and coastal viewpoints.

name: Taganga Bay
shortDescription: Coastal bay and village known for boat trips and water activities.
longDescription: A classic base for snorkeling and boat rides, with a relaxed seaside vibe and sunset viewpoints nearby.

name: Mirador de Taganga
shortDescription: Viewpoint overlooking Taganga Bay and the coastline.
longDescription: A quick stop for panoramic photos, especially at sunset. Bring water and go with enough daylight for the return.

name: Bahía Concha
shortDescription: Beach-area destination near Tayrona with a laid-back vibe.
longDescription: A popular beach day option with calmer water depending on conditions. Great for a relaxed outing from the city.

name: Tayrona National Natural Park (Parque Tayrona)
shortDescription: Top nature destination with beaches, trails, and biodiversity.
longDescription: Colombia’s most famous coastal national park near Santa Marta. Plan early entry, hydration, and sun protection. Trails connect beaches and viewpoints.

name: Playa Cristal
shortDescription: Clear-water beach in the Tayrona area, ideal for swimming.
longDescription: Known for transparent water and a calmer swimming feel on good days. Usually visited by boat and often requires planning around access rules.

name: Playa Cabo San Juan del Guía
shortDescription: Iconic Tayrona beach area with viewpoints and bays.
longDescription: One of the most famous spots inside Tayrona, with postcard views and trail connections. Best started early due to hiking time and heat.

name: Minca
shortDescription: Cooler mountain village for coffee, nature, and views.
longDescription: A popular escape from the heat with trails, waterfalls, viewpoints, and coffee experiences. Great for a day trip or 1–2 nights.

name: Pozo Azul (Minca)
shortDescription: Popular waterfall stop near Minca.
longDescription: A classic nature stop for a refreshing break. Conditions vary by season, so check local advice before going.

name: Cascadas de Marinka
shortDescription: Nature park with waterfalls and jungle scenery near Minca.
longDescription: A well-known waterfall area with trails and viewpoints. Combine with Minca for a full-day mountain itinerary.

name: Ciudad Perdida (Teyuna)
shortDescription: Archaeological site reached by multi-day trek in the Sierra Nevada.
longDescription: A world-famous trekking experience that requires a guided multi-day route. Best planned with reputable operators and proper preparation.
address: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Magdalena

name: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta
shortDescription: Mountain range and biosphere region behind Santa Marta.
longDescription: The dramatic mountain backdrop of the region, home to Indigenous communities, major ecosystems, and routes to places like Minca and Ciudad Perdida.
address: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia
